objective: Replace Alpine Loop with the smallest trustworthy app that finds useful constraint-based loop hikes, proven on real Washington data.

baseline.method: Physical lines in first-party tracked .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.py/.sh/.css files; exclude public vendored assets, .agents, .test/.spec files, tests/, testing/, __fixtures__/, and test-helpers.ts. Include application, preparation, research, scripts, and root code configuration. Normal readable formatting required.

experience: all meaningfully different routes available through paging; no per-start result cap
adjustable maximum road distance and share; trails remain the main experience
retain road connections needed to make a valid loop; do not choose unnecessary road detours solely to reach the minimum hike length
combine small path and road permutations before result storage; choose alternative starts in hike details
setup: no user source processing or API keys
quality: 20 frozen real queries across 3 contrasting Washington areas

performance.priority: User clarified 2026-09-30: longer searches are acceptable. Timing is descriptive; do not complicate architecture or cut exploration to chase sub-10-second results.

acceptance.engineering: Challenge raw sources, processing and storage from first principles. Prioritize robust code over patchwork tests; use targeted independent checks with restraint.
deferred: Hosted URL: user explicitly deferred hosting on 2026-09-30 to focus on an excellent local app that can be hosted later.

state: The local desktop area/constraints, progressive comparison, hike/start/direction details, GPX and browser reconnect work. Maintained app and preparation code is 5,187 lines versus the 24,063-line baseline. Cascades data remains installed. The isolated replacement solver is not ready: all 24 frozen queries were measured in guarded up-to-30-second observations, but only one of seven independently eligible source hikes was recovered at its original start. All seven source hikes use trails only. Two baseline observations exceeded the 1 GB sampled-memory guard. A conservative road-distance reachability bound passes existing independent preservation checks and lowers memory in one controlled pair, but still finds no Stevens route within that observation. Minor trail alternatives remain separate search branches, with grouping afterward. Production remains unchanged. Statewide preparation, fresh-source validation and automatic fresh-machine data acquisition remain unfinished. Hosting is deferred and public data publication is not approved.

roadConnectionPolicy.userDecision: A longer road connection stays when it enables a valid loop, including the Pratt example. Reject extra road walking chosen solely to pad minimum hike mileage.
roadConnectionPolicy.comparison: Compare connections in the context of the same start and substantial trail itinerary. Preserve legal direction, allowed access, loop/lollipop structure, repetition and the user's road limits. A globally shortest endpoint path can conflict with the rest of the hike; it is not a safe unconditional replacement.
roadConnectionPolicy.savedPrattEvidence: All 1,137 saved walks remain valid and satisfy the original constraints after replacing their connector runs with shortest directed paths while preserving the start and checking the complete walk. This yields 211 ordered trail-itinerary/start choices. Roads remain necessary: the replacements still contain 4.960–7.296 km of road. This is a property of this saved set, not a completeness proof or a count of meaningfully different hikes.

solverResearch.status: Unintegrated research candidate. Broad guarded baseline exposes insufficient original-start/family recovery, variable memory consumption and generation of minor trail alternatives. A road-bound correction preserves the existing tiny/source gates but does not resolve discovery.
solverResearch.recommendation: Keep this candidate out of the active app. Necessary road-assisted loops remain. Resolve generation of minor trail alternatives and useful itinerary discovery; validate sustained original-start/family recovery and runtime memory before replacing the solver.
solverResearch.correctnessBoundary: Preserve a qualifying realization for each explicitly defined hike class and eligible start. Shortest-only or ordinary Pareto-minimal local replacement is unsafe with minimum distance and climb. Resource intervals can reject impossibility but cannot establish a feasible combination. Preserve internal starts, complete internal loops, legal reversible stems, direction, access and simplicity; leave ambiguous regions uncollapsed.
experiments: Independent small networks with 10 and 20 local binary alternatives: measure search states and fully realized combinations, including a longer-only qualifying realization.
Recover the independently reconstructed Pratt, Franklin Falls, Annette-area and Talapus witnesses; retain eligible starts and qualifying directions.
Check internal starts, asymmetric access, longer-only qualifying lollipop stems, overlapping alternatives and road bypasses.
Measure real-query search work and discovery coverage, not merely reduced stored results. No first-N cap and no completeness claim based on heuristic failure to find more routes.

sources.title: Modeling the Variety of Trip Opportunities in Recreational Route Networks
sources.lesson: Raw trip counts suffer combinatorial explosion and overstate recreational variety. Useful product framing and coverage metrics, not a complete solver for our directed gain-constrained problem.

sources.title: A Linear Time Implementation of SPQR-Trees
sources.lesson: Separation pairs and virtual-edge skeletons give a structural basis for two-boundary bundles. Decomposition does not decide hike equivalence or justify discarding metric alternatives.

sources.title: Improved Alternative Route Planning
sources.lesson: Alternative graphs and rejoin penalties address repeated tiny detours during generation. Road A-to-B and near-shortest assumptions do not transfer as exhaustive constrained-loop guarantees.

sources.title: Finding k-shortest paths with limited overlap
sources.lesson: Monotone overlap permits early subtree pruning. Its similarity definition and shortest-prefix dominance differ from our present grouping and minimum resource requirements.

sources.title: Generating Constrained Length Personalized Bicycle Tours
sources.lesson: Reusable outbound trees and alternate returns generate closed tours within length intervals. The practical method is heuristic and does not certify all meaningful hike classes.

sources.title: Graphillion: Software Library Designed for Very Large Sets of Graphs in Python
sources.lesson: Frontier search and zero-suppressed decision diagrams represent path families without expanding every combination. Worth a separate bounded experiment only if simpler bundling fails; compression and directed lollipop encoding need validation.

sources.title: Finding All the Elementary Circuits of a Directed Graph
sources.lesson: Output-sensitive cycle enumeration still pays for every minor-variant cycle. Shared cycle discovery can reduce repeated work across starts but does not alone address this failure.
